results.basis: SELF-DECLARED: ESA 2010's own Annex A, Chapter 2, on the classification of local KAUs into industries — the document is Regulation (EU) No 549/2013, published by ESA 2010's own publisher, the European Parliament and the Council. This CLOSES a lead open since the esa2010-methodology-stack round, which recorded the edge `no-node-yet` because no NACE node existed; `nace-rev2` was minted in the Poland round on 2026-09-11 and the note is rewritten `resolved` in that file. The quote chosen is Annex A 2.147's flat statement rather than Annex A 1.22 ('The ESA 2010 contains EU-specific classifications, e.g. ... NACE Rev. 2 for industries'), which the live `esa-2010 -> cpa` edge already cites and which qualifies its own claim with a parenthetical about harmonisation. Relationship type is `methodology_depends_on` rather than the `legal_basis` the sibling `esa-2010 -> cpa` edge carries: NACE is the classification ESA's industry accounts are built on, not the act ESA rests on. ROUTE: EUR-Lex answers this container with an AWS WAF challenge (HTTP 202, zero bytes) on every legal-content URL tried, so the act was read from CELLAR, the Publications Office's own repository. The cited URL is the one an `Accept: application/xhtml+xml` + `Accept-Language: eng` negotiation on `publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/<CELEX>` RESOLVES to — a `resource/cellar/<uuid>/DOC_1` document a plain GET reads with no header at all, which is what a later grader run will issue. First-party publisher, direct read, no archive in the chain; `playbook/corpus-route.md`'s B cap is for archived snapshots and does not apply. QUOTE SHAPE, AND WHY IT IS TWO FRAGMENTS: the second fragment alone graded B `artefact-named-elsewhere-in-document` at coverage 1.0. `nace-rev2`'s title-lead is 'NACE Rev. 2', which `tokenise` reduces to three tokens, and the run rule needs about seven contiguous words of the full title — so a window carrying only the short name cannot name the target however clearly a reader sees it. The first fragment is Annex A 1.19's statement that the ESA employs the classification, and it carries the statutory name in full. WORTH KNOWING BEFORE ANYONE RE-READS THIS: ESA 2010 writes that name as 'Statistical classification of economic activities in the European UNION', while the node carries 'European COMMUNITY', which is Regulation (EC) No 1893/2006's own wording and the right title for the node. The run rule clears the 60% bar on the eight words the two spellings share, so the mismatch costs nothing here — but a future edge resting on a shorter span of that name may land on the wrong side of it. Both fragments are from the same act and neither is doing work the other could not check: the first names the artefact, the second states what ESA uses it for. Graded A, `quote-found-artefact-named`, on a live re-fetch 2026-09-15.

targetReport.title: NACE Rev. 2 — Statistical Classification of Economic Activities in the European Community
title_aliases: Statistical Classification of Economic Activities in the European Community
targetReport.publisher: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
targetReport.description: The EU's statutory industry classification, established by Regulation (EC) No 1893/2006 and derived from ISIC. Every EU member state's national activity classification is built on it; Poland's PKD 2007 is the first one wired here. Minted 2026-09-11 in the Poland round — the corpus had ISIC, NAICS, ANZSIC and CPA but no NACE node at all, despite 21 EU countries in the graph.
targetReport.cadence_note: Revised about once a generation (Rev. 1 1990, Rev. 1.1 2002, Rev. 2 2006, Rev. 2.1 2023); 0.05 is that rate written as a number.

ESA 2010 itself — Regulation (EU) No 549/2013, Annex A — lists COPNI among the functional classifications it uses, ¶23.05, and ¶22.17 says 'For describing and analysing the expenditure of private non-profit institutions serving households, COPNI is used.' ¶23.01 adds that the ESA's classifications are 'fully in line with' COPNI among others. targetReport.title: Classification of the Purposes of Non-Profit Institutions Serving Households (COPNI)
targetReport.description: The United Nations classification of the outlays of non-profit institutions serving households by purpose. One of the four classifications of expenditure according to purpose published together as Statistical Papers Series M No. 84 (ST/ESA/STAT/SER.M/84), with COFOG, COICOP and COPP. UNSD's classification registry records it as operational, adopted 1999 and published 2000 (read 2026-10-24, HTTP 200). Minted 2026-10-24: Uzbekistan's national-accounts sheet names it beside COICOP and COFOG, which closed the `uz-national-accounts -> COPNI` lead.
targetReport.cadence_note: Not a periodic release. Adopted 1999, published 2000 in Series M No. 84; no later revision is recorded in the registry.
